intro: Chennai's eight zones run from the old southern coast at Mylapore and Adyar, through T Nagar and Anna Nagar in the centre-west, to the OMR IT corridor, the Velachery and Tambaram side, and the western and northern belts out to Avadi and Royapuram. Housing-board layouts with numbered streets, such as Besant Nagar, Anna Nagar, Ashok Nagar and KK Nagar, make homes easy to find, while the OMR is mostly flats and gated campuses where a resident approves each visitor. Rail is a real advantage here: the suburban lines, the MRTS and the Blue and Green metro lines let a tutor cross the city without a car, though Medavakkam, Pallikaranai and most of the OMR still rely on roads.

Many of the city's children study under the Tamil Nadu State Board. The Directorate of Government Examinations conducts the SSLC public examination in Class 10 and the Higher Secondary examination, usually called +2, at the end of Class 12, and one of its seven regional offices is in Chennai. Its sample question papers set out each pattern, for example a three-hour, 100-mark SSLC Mathematics paper, and papers come in Tamil and English versions, so a tutor should know which one the child writes. Practical examinations come in February, before the theory papers. Families also follow CBSE, CISCE's ICSE and ISC, and IB or IGCSE.

Home work and online work fit together easily in Chennai. When a family in Velachery sends a request, the shortlist of two or three tutors starts with tutors in Velachery, then others in the same zone, then the rest of Chennai, then online tutors anywhere in India. Families see each tutor's fee before the free first demo and can switch later at no charge. A tutor near a suburban or MRTS station can cover a long stretch of line, while on the OMR, where many evenings are taken by office traffic, an online session for doubts can keep a student's week on track.

zone_notes.Adyar, Besant Nagar & Mylapore: The MRTS is the main rail link, with Thirumayilai and Mandaveli for Mylapore, Kasturba Nagar and Indira Nagar for Adyar, and Thiruvanmiyur for Besant Nagar, plus Teynampet on the Blue Line for Alwarpet. Mylapore's old houses sit on narrow lanes near the temple tank, so festival days there are better handled with a morning or online lesson.
zone_notes.T Nagar, Nungambakkam & Kodambakkam: Suburban trains stop at Nungambakkam, Kodambakkam, Mambalam and Saidapet, and a tutor arriving by train is usually more punctual than one driving into these dense, market-led streets. Parking a car is hard in West Mambalam and old T Nagar, and shopping weekends and festival seasons slow every route in.
zone_notes.Velachery, Guindy & Tambaram: Three rail systems serve parts of this zone: the Blue Line at Guindy and Alandur, the MRTS through Velachery to St Thomas Mount, and suburban trains along GST Road to Chromepet and Tambaram. Medavakkam and Pallikaranai have no station yet, so tutors there usually live nearby and ride a two-wheeler, and Kathipara and GST Road are heavy at office hours.
zone_notes.OMR & ECR: Gated communities along the OMR often want a resident to approve each visitor, so being added once as a regular guest in the society app saves time at every lesson. Only Perungudi has a station and the Purple Line is still being built, so tutors here travel by two-wheeler, bus or cab, and online sessions help on the busiest evenings.
zone_notes.Anna Nagar, Kilpauk & Aminjikarai: Anna Nagar's grid of numbered avenues makes homes quick to find, and Green Line stations from Thirumangalam to Shenoy Nagar and Arumbakkam put most of the zone within a short walk. Parking is limited near the 2nd Avenue shops and Purasawalkam's market streets, so book slots before the early-evening rush.
zone_notes.Vadapalani, KK Nagar & Porur: Vadapalani and Ashok Nagar are on the Green Line and KK Nagar's numbered sectors are easy to navigate, but west of Vadapalani there is no working metro yet, so homes along Arcot Road and in Porur rely on bus or road travel. Tutors who live along Arcot Road or in Porur suit this side, outside office hours at Porur Junction.
zone_notes.Mogappair, Ambattur & Avadi: The suburban line towards Arakkonam, with stations at Pattaravakkam, Ambattur, Annanur and Avadi, is the backbone, and a train plus short auto is the steadiest way to reach most homes. Defence areas and gated estates in Avadi may need entry details in advance, and Mogappair relies on Thirumangalam metro station or buses.
zone_notes.Perambur, Kolathur & North Chennai: Suburban trains serve Perambur, Villivakkam and Tondiarpet, and the Blue Line reaches Washermanpet and Tondiarpet, so a tutor without a car can work much of this zone. Older lanes are narrow and parking is tight near the markets, so a door number with a landmark helps, and newer buildings take your name at the gate.

boards: In Chennai you will teach Tamil Nadu State Board students for the SSLC and the Higher Secondary years, CBSE students, ICSE and ISC candidates, and some IB and IGCSE learners. For the state papers, read the time table, notifications and sample question papers through the Directorate of Government Examinations site and its notification portal. CBSE material is on the CBSE academic site and ICSE and ISC regulations on the CISCE site. Make your profile clear about the board you teach and whether you work with the Tamil or the English version of the state papers.
faqs: How does a family in Chennai find me as a tutor?

Families send one request with the class, board, subjects, locality and timings. NXTutors looks for tutors in that locality first, then in its zone, then across Chennai, then online, and offers two or three. Clear localities and boards on your profile, such as State Board SSLC or CBSE Class 12, help the match go your way.
Could I take only online students while living in Chennai?

You can. Some tutors prefer not to travel and list online lessons only; others teach at home in their own zone and online beyond it. Online profiles appear after local tutors when a family asks for home tuition, but families looking specifically for an online teacher can be matched with you from anywhere.
Which parts of Chennai make sense for home visits?

Start from your nearest station. A tutor beside the suburban line can reach Mambalam, Saidapet and Chromepet, and one near the Green Line covers Anna Nagar and Vadapalani. The OMR and Medavakkam depend on roads, so list them only if you can travel there regularly at the time lessons usually happen.
What identity checks do tutors go through?

Tutors who join go through an ID check. You verify your phone or email using a one-time code and upload a government photo ID; the team reviews it before your profile is published, and real tutors who pass show a Verified badge. This is an identity check only, not a background check; see /how-we-verify-tutors.
Where can I see the tutor plans?

All tutor plans, and what each includes, are on /pricing. Your hourly fee is separate and is yours to set; the family sees it before a free first demo, and a family that later wants a different tutor can switch at no charge, so the plan you choose and the fee you charge are independent decisions.
